title: Smooth Reading · Q2 W05 D02
objective: Read grade-level sentences accurately, smoothly, and with meaning.
introduction: Milo is reading a story aloud! Read the words clearly, pause at the punctuation, and let your voice show the meaning.

vocabulary.definition: Stop briefly at a punctuation mark when reading aloud.

Read words together in meaningful groups.

items.prompt: When you read a sentence aloud smoothly, what should you do?

options.text: Read in a flat, sleepy voice
Read as fast as you can
Read at a steady pace with meaning

items.explanation: Smooth, meaningful reading uses a steady pace so every word is read accurately and clearly.

options.text: Ana reads with expression, pausing at the period.
Ana whispers so no one hears.
Ana reads without looking at the words.

items.explanation: Reading with meaning means using expression and pausing at end marks, just like talking.

items.prompt: How should you read this sentence aloud: 'Look out!'?
items.explanation: An exclamation point shows strong feeling, so read it with an excited voice.

items.prompt: How should you read a question aloud?

options.text: With a rising voice at the end

items.explanation: Questions end with a question mark — your voice rises at the end, just like asking in real life.

items.prompt: Which reading sounds accurate and smooth?

options.text: Reading only the first word of each line
Reading every word at an even pace

items.explanation: Accurate, smooth reading reads every word correctly at an even pace without guessing.
